The proposed answer is $f(n)=\frac{n+1}{3}$, which matches the known result as I recall it. I could not verify the citation against the source, so this rests on memory of the literature rather than a checked proof.

The key claim is that for sufficiently large $n$, every edge-colored triangle-free graph of order $n$ with $\delta^c(G)\ge \frac{n+1}{3}$ contains a rainbow $C_4$, and this bound is sharp. The form $\frac{n+a}{b}$ fits with $a=1$ and $b=3$. The plausibility check also holds: a color-degree threshold near $n/3$ is the natural scale for triangle-free graphs, since $K_{n/2,n/2}$-type constructions with about $n/3$ colors per vertex can avoid rainbow $C_4$ and show the bound cannot be lowered much.

The final line "$n/3 + 1/3$" is the same expression as $\frac{n+1}{3}$, so it is consistent.
